flashcards.q: What are Cloud Run's two CPU allocation modes and what's the consequence of each?
flashcards.a: 'CPU only allocated during request processing' (default): throttles CPU to near-zero once no requests are in-flight, enabling scale-to-zero cost but silently starving detached background work after a response returns. 'CPU always allocated': behaves like an always-on box, billed continuously, background work keeps running.

flashcards.q: Why does Cloud Run scale to zero in a way Fargate structurally cannot match?
flashcards.a: Cloud Run's front door is an always-available request router that can hold an incoming request while spinning up a fresh instance on demand. Fargate has no built-in wake-on-request mechanism -- scaling to zero requires explicit Auto Scaling config, and scaling back up requires an external trigger, with a cold path (ENI + image pull) of tens of seconds to minutes.

flashcards.q: What is Cloud Run's default and maximum per-instance concurrency?
flashcards.a: Default 80 simultaneous requests per instance, configurable up to 1,000 per instance. Higher concurrency only helps for I/O-bound workloads; CPU-bound work contends for the same instance's CPU allocation at high concurrency.

flashcards.q: How long does Cloud Run keep an idle instance warm before tearing it down?
flashcards.a: Up to 15 minutes (10 minutes for GPU-backed instances) after the last request, then the instance is torn down back to zero.

flashcards.q: Contrast Cloud Functions 1st gen and 2nd gen (Cloud Run functions).
flashcards.a: 1st gen: bespoke pre-Cloud-Run engine, exactly 1 request per instance, max 9-minute timeout. 2nd gen: built on Cloud Run, concurrency up to 1,000/instance, up to 60-minute timeout, uses Eventarc triggers. Use 2nd gen for anything new.

flashcards.q: What's the difference between a direct Eventarc event and an audit-log-derived event, and which should you prefer?
flashcards.a: Direct events are emitted natively by ~100+ first-party GCP sources through a purpose-built stream, low latency. Audit-log-derived events are sourced from Cloud Audit Logs -- broader coverage (any API call) but more delivery lag. Prefer direct events whenever the source offers one.

flashcards.q: Does setting minScale >= 1 on a Cloud Run service eliminate all cold starts?
flashcards.a: No. It eliminates baseline cold starts for traffic within the warm instances' capacity, but a sudden spike beyond that capacity still triggers new cold-start instances to handle the overflow.

flashcards.q: What is the current recommended status of App Engine for new projects?
flashcards.a: App Engine is in maintenance mode and not recommended for new projects -- Cloud Run is its explicit successor for nearly every use case App Engine Standard used to serve.

flashcards.q: When should you choose GKE Autopilot over Cloud Run for a stateless-looking workload?
flashcards.a: Once it needs arbitrary long-lived non-HTTP TCP protocols, StatefulSet-style stable identity/persistent storage, complex sidecars beyond Cloud Run's limited multi-container support, or fine-grained custom scheduling/affinity -- capabilities Cloud Run doesn't offer natively.

flashcards.q: Why did Google rebuild Cloud Functions 2nd gen on top of Cloud Run instead of maintaining a separate engine?
flashcards.a: To converge scaling/cold-start engineering into one shared runtime -- every Cloud Run improvement automatically benefits Cloud Run functions -- while keeping the lighter function-first deployment experience as a product-level (not runtime-level) differentiator.
